<!-- fallback-svg:end -->
<ol>
<li>An equation is a balance: 100 + 72 + 14 + g = 331 gives g = 145 MW.</li>
<li>One equation with two unknowns, x + y = 145, has a whole line of answers.</li>
<li>An inequality keeps the line and one side of it: x + y ≥ 145 keeps the side away from the origin, the point (0, 0).</li>
<li>Multiplying by −1 flips the sign: x + y ≥ 145 is the same rule as −x − y ≤ −145.</li>
<li>Rules hold together: with x ≤ 130, y ≤ 100, x ≥ 0 and y ≥ 0, the plans that pass form a triangle.</li>
<li>Above the line, gas makes more than 145 MW; the extra is matched by spilling wind or sun. The ramp rule limits only the climb from 90 MW.</li>
</ol>
<p class="lx-hint">With JavaScript on, you work through this step by step on a live plane.</p>

<li>The plant limits and the 90 MW the combined-cycle plant made at 18:00 are illustrative.</li>

::: {#explain .lx-sec}
::: {.lx-sec-h}
## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="k4-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Equation (=)</dt><dd>Exactly: on the plane, the line only. In a model: a balance, such as supply equals demand.</dd>
<dt>Inequality (≤, ≥)</dt><dd>At most or at least: the line and one side. In a model: limits such as plant size or ramp.</dd>
<dt>Strict inequality (&lt;, &gt;)</dt><dd>One side without its line; models avoid it, because a best plan may not exist.</dd>
<dt>Flip rule</dt><dd>Multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number flips the sign.</dd>
<dt>Feasible region</dt><dd>The plans that pass every rule at once.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>Why a rule with two unknowns is a straight line</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Rearrange.** $x + y = 145$ becomes $y = 145 - x$.
- **Slope.** Each extra MW from the combined-cycle plant means one MW less from the peaker: the line falls one step for each step right, slope $-1$.
- **Intercept.** At $x = 0$ the line crosses the $y$ axis at 145.
- **Any rule.** $a_1 x + a_2 y = b$, with $a_1$ and $a_2$ not both 0. If $a_2 \neq 0$ it becomes $y = (b - a_1 x)/a_2$: a straight line with slope $-a_1/a_2$.
- **Vertical boundaries.** If $a_2 = 0$, the boundary is vertical: $x \le 130$ keeps the line $x = 130$ and everything to its left.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Many rules at once, as one table (a preview)</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Decisions:** the two outputs, $x$ and $y$.
- **Rules:** each of step 6's five inequalities becomes one row of a table, all written as ≤ (the ≥ rules flipped).
- **In one line:** the rows stack into $A x \le b$, with $A$ holding the numbers in front of $x$ and $y$, and $b$ the limits.
- **Where next:** [Bridge B1](b01-algebra-to-lp.html) builds this table from a word problem and hands it to a real solver; toolbox [K6](k06-vectors-matrices.html) covers vectors and matrices.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

## Check yourself
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="k4-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="neg" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Multiplying a rule by −1 changes which plans pass it.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. The sign flips as well, so −x − y ≤ −145 passes exactly the plans that x + y ≥ 145 passes.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="line" data-answer="fact">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A plan exactly on the line x + y = 145 passes the rule x + y ≥ 145.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Fact. ≥ means “at least”, so exactly 145 MW is allowed; only a strict &gt; would leave the line out.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="k4">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="pass" data-answer="b">
<p class="lx-qtext">Which plan passes both x ≤ 130 and x + y ≥ 145?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">x = 120, y = 20</li><li data-value="b">x = 130, y = 15</li><li data-value="c">x = 140, y = 10</li><li data-value="d">x = 100, y = 40</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>x = 130, y = 15: 130 ≤ 130 and 130 + 15 = 145 ≥ 145. The others give 140 MW in total, or break the 130 MW limit.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="solve" data-answer="c">
<p class="lx-qtext">Solve 3x − 20 ≥ 40.</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">x ≤ 20</li><li data-value="b">x ≥ 6.7</li><li data-value="c">x ≥ 20</li><li data-value="d">x ≤ −20</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>x ≥ 20: add 20 to both sides (3x ≥ 60), then divide by 3, a positive number, so the sign stays.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div id="k4-drill"></div>
```
